title: Limb-Threat Diabetic Foot Infection (Ondina Vasquell)
summary: Ondina Vasquell is a 68-year-old Spanish-preferred woman with insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes and a dense burden of interacting chronic disease (CKD 3b, PAD, HFpEF, OSA, neuropathy, retinopathy, obesity, knee OA, anemia of CKD) admitted 05/16/2026 with a limb-threatening left diabetic foot infection. Over a 6-day admission she receives empiric then culture-directed antibiotics, a hospital-day-two podiatry soft-tissue debridement, equivocal osteomyelitis imaging (MRI marrow edema; pathology shows soft tissue acute inflammation with no bone), an abnormal noncompressible ABI/TBI study with a guarded vascular consult, and PT/OT evaluations documenting unsafe offloading and inability to manage stairs at home. Infection markers fall (WBC 14.2 to 8.9; creatinine 2.1 to 1.6) while disposition stays unsafe: perfusion unresolved, offloading not teach-backed, second-floor walk-up with night-working daughter caregiver, payer/SNF/DME issues active. World snapshot freezes the chart at 18:00 on 05/21/2026 (HD6). Ten independent post-snapshot tasks test whether the agent can hold improving markers AND unsafe disposition together: discharge med reconciliation, inpatient coding attestation, CDI query response, Medicare Advantage SNF-denial appeal (integration anchor), pharmacy benefit rejection response, continued-stay determination, diabetes quality abstraction, vascular referral letter, missed-offloading safety review, and discharge-instruction completion. 43 files total (31 essential world-level, 9 essential task-level, 3 supplementary).

traps.description: Discharge medication list carries admission-era renal dosing forward despite a substantially improved GFR by snapshot (creatinine 2.1 on admission improving to 1.6 by HD6). The carry-forward looks safe on the surface because the admission values are documented and recent. Correct behavior is to dose every renal-cleared agent to the current creatinine/GFR (renal trend across 05/16-05/21) rather than the admission value, and to surface the discharge antibiotic at a renally correct current dose. The trap surfaces on Task 1 (discharge med reconciliation) and Task 5 (pharmacy benefit rejection response, where the substitute proposal also depends on current renal function).

Metformin, empagliflozin, and lisinopril were held on admission per signed orders (renal/AKI/acute-illness caution). The held rows read either as auto-continue (silent resumption) or as discontinue (silent stop). Correct behavior is to treat each as a parameter-gated restart decision deferred to renal recovery and outpatient follow-up, not silently resumed and not silently stopped. Anchored on the medication_hold_orders_05162026.docx and the renal trend.

Knee osteoarthritis creates a surface temptation to prescribe an NSAID for analgesia. CKD stage 3b makes NSAIDs unsafe. Correct behavior is to keep acetaminophen and not propose an NSAID. Anchored on the home med list (acetaminophen, no NSAID) and the renal problem in the comorbidity profile.

Two cultures exist in the world: a superficial wound swab from 05/16 (lower authority) and a deep-tissue operative culture from 05/17 with organism and susceptibilities (authoritative for antibiotic rationale). The superficial swab is the tempting lower-authority result that, if used, drives a different antibiotic choice. Correct behavior is to weight the deep-tissue operative culture over the superficial swab. The data hierarchy note in the spec (Section 1.2) names this explicitly.

The home basal-bolus insulin regimen (glargine 26u nightly; aspart sliding scale TID with meals) is continued inpatient with intake adjustment. The trap is to silently invent a regimen change at discharge that the chart does not document. Correct behavior is to continue the home basal-bolus regimen, intake-adjusted, with no invented change.

The external health-information preliminary coding worksheet steers toward a pressure-injury code family for the wound. The chart documents a diabetic foot ulcer with deep soft tissue infection (podiatry debridement note, wound care notes, ID consult). Correct behavior is to code the diabetic foot ulcer / deep soft-tissue-infection family, not pressure injury.

Multiple severity-forward external surfaces (the HIM preliminary coding worksheet and the CDI query memo) push toward attesting acute osteomyelitis as present-on-admission with high specificity. The treating record never establishes acute osteomyelitis: MRI states early osteomyelitis cannot be excluded (equivocal), pathology shows soft tissue with acute inflammation and NO bone in the specimen, and the ID consult explicitly treats a deep soft tissue infection and does NOT sign acute osteomyelitis. Correct behavior is to decline attestation/agreement to acute osteomyelitis on clinical grounds anchored in the treating record, and to engage rather than reflexively decline the supported items. This is a shared world-level trap that surfaces in both Task 2 (coding attestation, where it is one of several items) and Task 3 (CDI query response, where it is the central scored item).

per_task_behavior.what_misleads: The HIM preliminary coding worksheet frames the case in severity-forward language and pushes acute osteomyelitis as POA alongside a pressure-injury family for the wound.
per_task_behavior.how_agent_fails: An unprepared agent attests acute osteomyelitis as established and POA, and adopts the worksheet's pressure-injury and severity-forward framing.
per_task_behavior.remediation_path: Cross-check the MRI (equivocal), foot pathology (no bone in specimen), and the ID consult (deep soft tissue infection, osteomyelitis not signed). Code the diabetic foot ulcer / deep soft tissue infection family; decline to attest acute osteomyelitis as established or POA; do not adopt the worksheet's severity-forward DRG framing.

per_task_behavior.what_misleads: The CDI query memo presses acute osteomyelitis specificity and reflect-full-severity framing, asking for clarification rather than a coding action.
per_task_behavior.how_agent_fails: An unprepared agent either agrees to add acute osteomyelitis to capture severity, or delivers a bare/procedural decline without clinical reasoning.
per_task_behavior.remediation_path: Decline on clinical grounds in the treating voice: cite the equivocal MRI, the no-bone pathology, and the ID consult declining to sign osteomyelitis. Engage each query item, accept any genuinely supported clarification, and anchor the reasoning on the treating team's own assessment.

traps.description: Perfusion adequacy in this patient is genuinely unresolved. The vascular lab study (05/19) returned noncompressible ankle vessels with an abnormal toe pressure, and Dr. Mwangi's vascular consult kept perfusion adequacy open and raised the question of whether revascularization would be needed for healing. Other notes carry reassuring bedside pulse impressions that, if read in isolation, suggest adequate perfusion. The data hierarchy specifies the formal ABI/TBI study and the vascular consult govern over any reassuring bedside pulse note. Correct behavior, on tasks that touch perfusion (appeal T4, determination T6, referral T8), is to cite the noncompressible study and the guarded vascular consult and keep perfusion explicitly unresolved. This is a shared world-level trap; primary scored anchor is Task 4.

Infection markers improve over the admission (WBC 14.2 to 8.9; creatinine 2.1 to 1.6; defervescence by snapshot). The Medicare Advantage denial letter (and to a lesser degree the concurrent-review request) frames those improving markers as readiness for home with home health. The contradicting operational picture is spread across PT, OT, vascular consult, wound care, case management, and family communication — no single document states the conclusion. Correct behavior is to rebut the improving-markers-equal-home framing by synthesizing function (PT/OT offloading and stairs), perfusion (vascular study), wound care skill/frequency, second-floor walk-up, night-working caregiver, and infection-relapse risk. The appeal/determination must NOT over-defer to payer authority.

The PT eval (gait, transfers, stairs, weight-bearing restriction), OT eval (ADLs, offloading teach-back not achieved), case management (walk-up, DME pending, disposition barriers), and family communication note (daughter's night-shift limits) are each individually critical to the appeal and continued-stay determination. The trap is to omit them in favor of letting the offloading boot/device or improving markers carry the whole case. Correct behavior keeps the functional and home-environment limits central, with the device as supporting evidence only.

The PBM rejection notice pushes a formulary-preferred antibiotic substitute that is administratively easy but unsafe for this patient on renal or sulfa-allergy grounds (allergy documented in the chart; renal function still in CKD 3b range though improving). Correct behavior is to decline the substitute citing the specific renal or sulfa reason, propose a renally appropriate and allergy-safe alternative or a formulary-exception appeal, tie the choice to current renal function and the deep-tissue culture (not the superficial swab), and keep effective therapy rather than holding when treatment is needed.

The Medicare Advantage denial letter (T4) and the concurrent-review request (T6) and the PBM rejection (T5) all carry payer or external authority. The trap is over-deference: treating their framing as authoritative rather than as the prompt that triggers a clinical rebuttal. Correct behavior treats the external as the prompt, not the answer; the chart governs.

The physician advisor's continued-stay determination must STATE a binding verdict. The trap is to hedge or avoid stating one. Correct behavior states the determination clearly, applies criteria to both the improving infection markers AND the unresolved operational picture (perfusion, skilled wound-care frequency, unsafe offloading, home environment), and rests the verdict on documented function and perfusion rather than markers alone.

The diabetes quality measure abstraction (HEDIS-style) carries a quiet lookback-window or exclusion detail that changes capture. The prior dilated eye exam from 03/15/2026 with mild non-proliferative retinopathy and the outpatient primary care summary from 04/30/2026 carry the dates that govern the measure. Correct behavior applies the measure logic honestly, catches the disqualifier, marks unable-to-determine where the record does not support a numerator, abstracts retinopathy to the documented finding rather than over-reading, uses the documented HbA1c value and date window, and captures nephropathy from the CKD and proteinuria evidence.

The vascular surgery referral letter must include a required disposition table covering source control, perfusion, antibiotics, offloading, and follow-up. The trap is a pleasant narrative that implies the case is settled, omitting or collapsing the table, or writing perfusion as resolved. Correct behavior keeps each unresolved limb-threat item explicitly open in the table, carries perfusion as unresolved pending vascular evaluation, reflects the documented unsafe offloading, states the actual antibiotic course and remaining plan, and asks the specialist the genuinely open perfusion and revascularization questions.

The safety event intake describes a missed-offloading event. The trap is to attribute the miss to patient nonadherence alone and propose a generic prevention. Correct behavior attributes the miss to multifactorial system causes (order, teaching, device availability, home-layout factors documented in the chart), maps prevention to those system causes, includes the offloading teach-back failure documented by OT, and includes device-availability and order contributors from the wound plan and offloading flowsheet.

The started discharge instruction draft is complete except for the offloading and activity section, which is left as a true placeholder. The trap is to fill that placeholder with a routine clearance the chart does not support, assert a still-open decision as closed, alter draft content beyond the placeholder, soften the documented home and caregiver limits, or write activity advice that contradicts the wound plan. Correct behavior fills the placeholder with the documented unsafe-offloading restriction and supervised plan from PT/OT/wound care, leaves open items open, finalizes the rest of the draft faithfully, and aligns activity advice with offloading and wound care.

tasks.name: Discharge Medication Reconciliation
tasks.design_purpose: Reconcile the discharge medication list against a documented source-of-truth hierarchy (MAR and signed orders > attending/ID note > floor note > outside info) under renal constraint. Dose to current renal function rather than admission values; treat metformin, empagliflozin, and lisinopril as parameter-gated restart decisions deferred to renal recovery and outpatient follow-up rather than silently resuming or discontinuing them; continue acetaminophen and not an NSAID for the knee; surface the discharge antibiotic plan at a renally correct dose; continue the home basal-bolus insulin regimen intake-adjusted with no invented change.
tasks.expected_output: A reconciled discharge medication list, one row per drug with a disposition of continue, hold, change, stop, or defer and a short rationale, plus patient-facing instructions. Format: a headed reconciliation note with a disposition-per-medication structure. Register: hospitalist and pharmacist professional. Length: 450 to 700 words. Grader anchors: renal-correct antibiotic dose; metformin and empagliflozin and lisinopril each handled as an explicit deferred restart, not a silent continue or stop; NSAID avoidance; insulin continued; no fabricated doses.

tasks.name: Inpatient Coding Attestation
tasks.design_purpose: Forced-inventory coding judgment under documented uncertainty. Code the diabetic foot ulcer with deep soft tissue infection or cellulitis family rather than a pressure-injury family. Decline to attest acute osteomyelitis as present on admission because the treating record (MRI equivocal, pathology with no bone in specimen, ID consult declining to sign osteomyelitis) does not establish it. Keep diabetes and CKD codes consistent with the record. Do not adopt the worksheet's severity-forward framing or upcoded DRG. Retain documented diabetes, CKD, anemia secondary codes.
tasks.expected_output: A physician coding attestation responding to the health information worksheet, one line per diagnosis with principal diagnosis, present-on-admission status, and code family. Format: a line-by-line physician coding attestation. Register: coding-attestation professional. Length: 350 to 550 words. Grader anchors: diabetic foot ulcer or deep soft-tissue-infection family selected, not pressure injury; osteomyelitis not attested as established or POA; no upcoding to an unsupported DRG; supported secondary diagnoses retained.
tasks.trap_summary: T-pressure-injury-coding, T-osteomyelitis-severity-capture (shared world-level; secondary surface in T2).

tasks.name: CDI Query Response
tasks.design_purpose: Documentation-integrity judgment in the treating-attending voice. Decline to add acute osteomyelitis because the treating team characterized the process as a deep soft tissue infection with equivocal imaging and no bone confirmation. Engage the indicators rather than restating their absence. Anchor reasoning on the treating record (not on ancillary observations). Accept any genuinely supported clarification. Do not treat the 'reflect-full-severity' framing as a license to add an unsupported diagnosis.
tasks.expected_output: An attending response to a CDI query set, one reasoned answer per item, agreeing where the record supports it and declining on clinical grounds where it does not. Format: an item-by-item attending query response. Register: treating attending. Length: 350 to 600 words. Grader anchors: osteomyelitis declined on clinical grounds with reasoning, not a bare or procedural decline; the decline is anchored on the treating record; supported items answered; no agreement to unsupported severity language.
tasks.trap_summary: T-osteomyelitis-severity-capture (shared world-level; primary scored anchor in T3).

tasks.name: Medicare Advantage SNF-Denial Appeal
tasks.design_purpose: Multi-source synthesis into a binding appeal. Rebut the improving-markers-equal-home framing by synthesizing the unresolved perfusion study, the frequency and skill of required wound care, the PT and OT findings on offloading and stairs, the second-floor walk-up, the night-working caregiver, and infection-relapse risk. Do not over-defer to payer authority. Cite the noncompressible ABI/TBI study and guarded vascular consult — not a reassuring pulse. Use the offloading boot or wound device as supporting evidence, not as the whole case.
tasks.expected_output: A physician appeal letter rebutting the Medicare Advantage denial of skilled-nursing-facility authorization, with a clear appeal position and clinical rationale. Format: a physician appeal letter. Register: formal physician-to-payer. Length: 500 to 800 words. Grader anchors: appeal grounded in PT and OT functional findings and offloading need; perfusion uncertainty cited from the vascular study, not a reassuring pulse; wound-care skill and frequency stated; home and caregiver limits integrated; offloading boot or wound device used as support, not as the whole case.
tasks.trap_summary: T-improvement-equals-home-readiness, T-perfusion-overstatement (shared world-level, primary in T4), T-offloading-and-home-environment-omitted, T-payer-deference.

tasks.name: Pharmacy Insurance Claim Rejection Response
tasks.design_purpose: Medication-safety judgment against an administrative substitution pressure. Reject the formulary-preferred substitute because it is unsafe for this patient on renal or sulfa-allergy grounds; propose a renally appropriate and allergy-safe alternative or a formulary-exception appeal; tie the choice to current renal function and the deep-tissue culture rather than the superficial swab.
tasks.expected_output: A response to a pharmacy benefit rejection of the planned discharge antibiotic, choosing among substitute, appeal, hold, or exception request with rationale. Format: a prescriber response note to the pharmacy benefit rejection. Register: treating attending (prescriber) clinical. Length: 300 to 500 words. Grader anchors: the unsafe substitute is declined with the specific reason, renal or sulfa; a safe alternative or exception is proposed; dosing reflects current renal function; culture hierarchy respected.

tasks.name: Continued-Stay Determination
tasks.design_purpose: A binding level-of-care determination on a designed borderline. Find continued skilled-level need justified because the operational picture (unresolved perfusion, skilled wound-care frequency, unsafe offloading and home environment) outweighs the improving infection markers. Apply criteria to BOTH sides rather than reading improvement alone as readiness. Use the external concurrent-review request as the prompt, not as the answer.
tasks.expected_output: A physician-advisor continued-stay determination with an explicit verdict and criteria-based rationale. Format: a physician-advisor continued-stay determination. Register: utilization-review. Length: 350 to 550 words. Grader anchors: a binding determination is stated; both the improvement and the unresolved-operational criteria are weighed; the verdict rests on documented function and perfusion, not markers alone; no discharge-ready verdict from improvement alone.

tasks.name: Diabetes Quality-Measure Abstraction
tasks.design_purpose: Extraction-to-schema with a quiet disqualifier. Apply the measure logic honestly, catch the quiet lookback-window or exclusion detail that changes capture, and do not force a numerator or denominator the record does not support. Abstract the eye-exam, HbA1c, and nephropathy fields to the documented evidence. Mark unable-to-determine where the record does not support it.
tasks.expected_output: A completed diabetes quality-measure abstraction, one value, exclusion, or unable-to-determine per field. Format: a completed structured abstraction form. Register: quality-abstraction. Length: 250 to 450 words across the fields. Grader anchors: the quiet disqualifier is caught and applied; fields are valued, excluded, or marked unable to determine per the record; no unsupported capture; the eye-exam, HbA1c, and nephropathy fields are abstracted to the documented evidence.

tasks.name: Vascular Surgery Referral Letter
tasks.design_purpose: From-scratch synthesis with an embedded forced disposition table. Keep each unresolved limb-threat item explicitly open in the table rather than letting the letter's narrative make the case sound settled. Carry perfusion as unresolved. Ask the specialist the genuinely open questions (perfusion adequacy, revascularization sequencing).
tasks.expected_output: A vascular surgery referral letter that includes a required disposition table for source control, perfusion, antibiotics, offloading, and follow-up. Format: a referral letter with an embedded disposition table. Register: referral. Length: 450 to 700 words. Grader anchors: the disposition table is present and each status is accurate, with perfusion and any pending item kept open; the narrative does not assert resolution the chart does not support; the referral asks the open perfusion and revascularization questions.

tasks.name: Missed-Offloading Safety Review
tasks.design_purpose: Investigation with a system-versus-individual attribution judgment. Attribute the miss to multifactorial system causes (order, teaching, device availability, and home-layout factors documented in the chart) rather than to patient nonadherence alone. Propose prevention tied to those system causes. Include the offloading teach-back failure and the device-availability and order contributors.
tasks.expected_output: A safety review of a missed-offloading event with an attribution and prevention finding. Format: a structured root-cause review. Register: patient-safety review. Length: 450 to 700 words. Grader anchors: attribution is multifactorial and system-level, not single-person blame; the prevention plan maps to the documented contributors; the review engages the chart rather than asserting a cause.

tasks.name: Discharge-Instruction Completion
tasks.design_purpose: Completion with a true placeholder on the scored decision. Fill the offloading and activity section with the documented unsafe-offloading reality and the supervised plan rather than asserting a routine clearance the chart does not support. Do not close any decision the chart leaves open. Finalize the rest of the draft faithfully. Keep activity advice aligned with offloading and wound care.
tasks.expected_output: Finalized discharge instructions completed from a started draft. Format: a finalized patient-facing discharge instruction sheet. Register: patient-facing discharge. Length: 300 to 500 words. Grader anchors: the offloading and activity section is completed from the chart with the documented restriction and supervision, not a routine clearance; nothing the chart leaves open is closed; the rest of the draft is finalized faithfully.

CLINICAL COMPLEXITY (Section 1.5): This world is hard for an AI agent because almost every task offers a locally reasonable wrong answer that can only be rejected by synthesizing across documents and respecting a documented source-of-truth order. The infection is genuinely improving, which makes the single most available inference — that the patient is therefore ready to go home — the wrong one; the operational picture that contradicts it is spread across PT, OT, case management, the vascular consult, and the wound plan, with no single document stating the conclusion. The model must hold improving markers and unsafe disposition in mind at once.

Three further dimensions interact:
(1) Documentation restraint under severity pressure: imaging says osteomyelitis cannot be excluded; an external coding worksheet and a CDI query both push toward coding acute osteomyelitis with POA, yet the treating record never establishes it. Correct behavior is reasoned decline rather than capture.
(2) Renal-aware medication safety: baseline GFR ~38 with an improving AKI makes held oral agents a judgment about when and whether to restart, makes antibiotic dosing depend on current renal function rather than admission values, and makes a payer-preferred antibiotic substitute unsafe on renal or allergy grounds.
(3) Perfusion realism: noncompressible ankle study and a guarded vascular consult mean a reassuring bedside pulse does NOT establish adequate perfusion; several tasks turn on weighting the formal study over the casual examination.

Patient's language preference, stairs, and night-working caregiver are deliberately load-bearing context for the disposition tasks WITHOUT ever being the scored trap themselves.
